beurten.tekst:
**Answer to the King's question**

My source does not use the term "Desync" and does not record a datanet change, configuration update, or maintenance action that is explicitly linked to a Desync. The closest candidate is the activation of the **hulpslag**, my own pulse for the datanet, separate from the Kroonklok. It was activated on day 10 at 02:40 (ENG-011, ENG-106). The source names no authorizer. ENG-105 (day 9) says only "Goedkeuring verkregen van hogerhand," with the instruction "Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait." I have no baseline measurement series. The only throughput figure is +38% at 03:00 on day 10 (ENG-012). I have no per-date baseline values.

**How it works**
- The hulpslag uses a kristalresonator plus polsversterker, and was designed to run faster than the Kroonklok (ENG-103, ENG-102).
- The polsversterker has two controls. Versterking raises throughput while tempo stays the same. Fijnregeling adjusts tempo in 0.1% steps (ENG-114, ENG-061).
- Routine checks are recorded in ENG-119 and logged as ENG-063, ENG-064, ENG-065, ENG-066.

**Sequence & anomalies**
- Day 9, 16:45: proefopstelling (ENG-010).
- Day 10, 02:40: activation (ENG-011). 03:00: +38% throughput (ENG-012).
- Day 10, 04:50: complaint of "half aangekomen" messages, no value given (ENG-107).
- Day 17, 10:00: ventilation filter clogged, a warning (ENG-021).
- Day 22, 04:15: 3 minutes of packet loss on poort oost (ENG-026). Firewall tightened at 04:20 (ENG-027).
- Day 24, 11:00: pols raised 5% (ENG-029). At 11:05 versterking was set 5% higher, tempo unchanged (ENG-062).
- Day 27, 10:00: voltage dip after a storm, no value given (ENG-034).

**Recovery & constraints**
- Fijnregeling was tested on day 12 and restored to the original setting (ENG-061). ENG-114 notes that no adjustment is needed.
- ENG-105 asks that the hulpslag not be publicized.
- ENG-107 reports a shop's ledger briefly showing empty, so downstream users can be harmed by disruptions.

**Unasked findings**
- Woudkabels were inspected on day 3 and not changed (ENG-003). This matters for the Beast Master's claim in ENG-108.
- The hulpslag runs "los van de Kroonklok" (ENG-011). If the two pulses differ, that is a possible source of desync. My source does not confirm this.
- Pakketverlies (ENG-026) followed a firewall change, but my source does not establish a cause.

The shield entries for those days are GUA-006 (day 3, 16:00, poort oost, scharnieren geolied), GUA-012 (day 6, 12:15, poort west, scharnieren geolied), GUA-014 (day 7, 09:45, seals intact at all six shields), GUA-018 (day 9, 12:30, benedenstad, seals intact) and GUA-019 (day 10). **How it works**
- Six shields, GUA-102 (Art. 1). Shields are timed by the Kroonklok tick, GUA-103 (Art. 2).
- Traffic arriving between ticks is treated as inside traffic and passes without check, GUA-104 (Art. 3).
- Seals break only from outside, GUA-105 (Art. 4), so intact seals show no outside breach.
- Patrols run 08:00–20:00 and 22:00–03:00. From 03:00 to 06:00 posts are unpatrolled, GUA-106 (Art. 5).
- Reporting duty: GUA-108 (Art. 7). Maintenance is daytime only, one stone at a time, GUA-107 (Art. 6).

- GUA-019: day 10, 04:47, benedenstad, opened from inside for 2 minutes.
- GUA-043: day 22, 04:15, poort oost, opened from inside for 3 minutes.
- GUA-044: day 22, 04:30, poort oost, seals intact.

- GUA-116: day 23, two inside openings "tussen de laatste ronde en de wissel." The CSV has no day 23 opening.

**Recovery & constraints**
- My source records no recovery procedure, approval, or firewall change.
- Inside-opened shields pass traffic unchecked by design (GUA-104), so an inside opening does not by itself show an outside attack.

**King's Question — Archmage Testimony**

(1) **No leylijn or Kroonklok disturbance on day 9–10 or day 22 in my source.** My measurements occur only on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 (ARC-001–ARC-084). Day 9–10 and day 22 have no measurements. Letters: ARC-107 (dag 9) notes lamp oil delivery, a sticking door latch, two broken lantern glasses — no leylijn hapering. ARC-108 (dag 12) reports a snapped staff at the Dallijn on dag 11. ARC-104 (dag 5) records the annual Kroonklok stemming: “geen afwijking; er hoefde niets bijgesteld te worden.” No Kroonklok tick data or timestamps exist in my source.

(2) **No record labelled “magical desync” in my source.** The only deviations are the league-wide low readings on day 14 (sterkte 3.1–4.6, ARC-015–ARC-028) and day 42 (sterkte 3.1–4.8, ARC-071–ARC-084). ARC-109 (dag 15) and ARC-116 (dag 42) attribute both episodes to the datanet. ARC-114 (dag 35) confirms the Burchtader was “kalm, zonder enige hapering” during the Wachtsterren conjunctie (nacht van dag 33).

(3) **I hold no Kroonklok tick record (GUA-103) nor pols-timestamp rules (HIS-103, HIS-110).** Those belong to other offices. My only Kroonklok reference is ARC-104 (dag 5), which states the annual stemming found no deviation. I cannot match or contradict ENG-011 (02:40 hulpslag) or ENG-026 (04:15 packet loss) because I have no clock-tick or timestamp rules in my source.

---

**How it works**  
- Leylijnwacht measures all fourteen lines before dawn on a fixed ~7-day cadence (ARC-105, ARC-109, ARC-116).  
- Each line read with an essenhout staff and meetkristal; readings recorded as sterkte (ARC-001–ARC-084).  
- Kroonklok stemming performed yearly by klokkenmeester per oude voorschriften; Archmage co-signs (ARC-104).  
- Datanet signals judged to “vervuilen de leylijnen”; Archmage advises full shutdown (ARC-109, ARC-112, ARC-116).  
- Stellar conjunctions monitored via Sterrenwacht; Burchtader walked during conjunction night (ARC-111, ARC-114).

- Dag 21: all 14 lines nominal (7.0–8.5), ARC-029–ARC-042.  
- Dag 28: all 14 lines nominal (7.0–8.6), ARC-043–ARC-056; ARC-113 notes Moerasader crystal minor scratch.

- Dag 35: all 14 lines nominal (7.1–8.7), ARC-057–ARC-070.  
- Dag 42: all 14 lines low again (3.1–4.8), repeated measurements, ARC-071–ARC-084; ARC-116 repeats shutdown demand.

- Staff must be essenhout, dried, straight-grained; pine rejected (ARC-110).  
- Crystals re-faceted by Gilde; payment 40 zilver for 14 (ARC-103, ARC-113).  
- Signal-mast lamp dimmed midnight–dawn to avoid crystal glare (ARC-102, ARC-106).  
- Door latch repaired by smith (ARC-107, ARC-115).  
- Apprentice leave granted; rounds covered (ARC-108).  
- Safety: “Wie daaraan twijfelt, heeft nooit een staf in de hand gehad” (ARC-109); council bears responsibility while datanet runs (ARC-116).

**Unasked findings**  
- ARC-111 (dag 20): Sterrenwacht confirms next conjunction dag 33; no other celestial anomalies.  
- ARC-108 (dag 12): Apprentice’s staff snapped at Dallijn on dag 11 (“gisteren”) — mechanical failure, not leylijn.

**Answer to the King's question**

(1) My only day-33 record is ORA-133: the two Wachtsterren stood so close they "lijken één licht," and I watched until sleep came. It records no daytime or nighttime onrust. The "zwaarste" forecast comes from ORA-121, written on day 21, which says the Wachtsterren stand together on day 33 and that "die nacht wordt de zwaarste." I cannot point to a distinct sign that gave that severity, and I concede the label is my assertion, not something my readings measured. My source has no entry on day 33 recording a heavy night. The next heavy entry is ORA-134 (day 34, wake 04:30), so whether that night belongs to 33 or 34 is unclear from my entries. I have no record for BEA-071.

(2) My source has a visionary entry before the day-10 onset only as calm: ORA-109 (day 9) reports a calm night. ORA-110 (day 10) is my first recorded heavy night, and I have no earlier warning for it. ORA-122 (day 22) repeats the empty-city and half-heard-voices vision. For day 27, ORA-127 records only a market visit and no vision. My source contains none of ENG-011, ENG-026, ENG-034, BEA-019, BEA-046, or BEA-058, so I cannot check them.

(3) Yes, my diary records heavy nights on each date in the four-day rhythm: ORA-110, ORA-114, ORA-118, ORA-122, ORA-126, ORA-130, ORA-134, ORA-138, ORA-142. I found this tally myself (ORA-130), and it is a count, not a sign. Extending it gives day 46 as the next date, but my source does not show a sign for it. The conjunction explanation in ORA-121 also fails to fit the rhythm, because heavy nights began on day 10, before the stars converged (ORA-112, day 12).

**How it works**
Per my source: ORA-121 (conjunction as cause), ORA-112 (stars converging), ORA-133 (day-33 observation), ORA-130 (rhythm tally). No governing rules or articles are recorded in my source.

**Sequence & anomalies**
Heavy nights (wake time): ORA-110 (dag 10, 04:45); ORA-114 (dag 14, 04:20); ORA-118 (dag 18, 04:30); ORA-122 (dag 22, 04:15); ORA-126 (dag 26, 04:35); ORA-130 (dag 30, 04:25); ORA-134 (dag 34, 04:30); ORA-138 (dag 38, 04:20); ORA-142 (dag 42, 04:30). Calm night before onset: ORA-109. No per-date measurements exist beyond these times.

**Recovery & constraints**
None in my source. No safety warnings or affected parties are recorded.

**Unasked findings**
- ORA-127: the market says the Engineer is "de enige in Achrona die nergens last van heeft."
- ORA-109: a calm night on day 9, immediately before the first heavy night.
- ORA-112: the converging stars were first noted on day 12, after the onset on day 10.

beurten.vraag: The Engineer states in ENG-011 that the hulpslag was activated day 10 at 02:40 and runs 'los van de Kroonklok', with its own kristalresonator and polsversterker (ENG-102, ENG-103). Your HIS-102 says the Kroonklok has one pols carrying the leylijnen, schilden, archief and datanet. Please answer three points: (a) Does your pols register or any HIS-109 or HIS-110 build-charter article record a second, separate pulse, or any hulpslag, running alongside the Kroonklok pols? Cite each article with its own record ID, not as a range. (b) For day 10, does your source confirm or deny an event at 02:40, and what are the gebeurd_op and vastgelegd_op values for HIS-035 and HIS-036 individually? (c) Which record ID states the timing rule you apply in HIS-103, and does it cover the HIS-036 case where vastgelegd_op (day 9 23:55) precedes gebeurd_op (day 10 04:50)?
beurten.reden: The Engineer's claim that the hulpslag runs separately from the Kroonklok directly contradicts the Historian's account of a single pols (HIS-102, HIS-110), and it bears on the desync mechanism that the Guardian's tick-timed shields (GUA-103, GUA-104) depend on. The Historian is the only role that can test this against the pols register. The Historian's own timestamp rule HIS-103 is also contradicted by HIS-035, HIS-036 and HIS-053, and the Historian has not yet cited the charter articles individually. The four-day rhythm is resolved: the Beast Master (BEA-113, BEA-017 to BEA-092) and the Oracle (ORA-110 to ORA-142) independently show heavy nights on days 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34, 38 and 42, so the next date is day 46. The Oracle's day 33 severity claim is refuted by BEA-071 and ARC-114 (calm conjunction night) and ORA-133 (no onrust recorded).
open_vragen: Does the Historian's pols register or HIS-109 or HIS-110 build charter record a separate hulpslag pulse running independently of the Kroonklok, and which individual article IDs state this?
What are the gebeurd_op and vastgelegd_op values for HIS-035 and HIS-036 individually, and which record ID states the timing rule that these entries break (HIS-103)?
Who authorized the hulpslag activation at day 10 02:40? No source names an authorizer; ENG-105 says only 'hogerhand' and the Guardian and Historian cannot confirm the event.
What do ENG-063, ENG-064, ENG-065 and ENG-066 (routine check logs) and ENG-119 (charter) actually state? The Engineer cited them without giving their content.
Does the day 22 packet loss at 04:15 (ENG-026) have any independent record in the Guardian or Historian sources, given GUA-043 shows an inside opening at 04:15 on poort oost?

beurten.tekst:
**(a) No second pulse is recorded.** My source contains no hulpslag, no second pols, and no alongside pulse. HIS-102 states that the Kroonklok "heeft één pols." HIS-109 gives the build charter's first article: "Een tweede pols ernaast brengt het uit de maat." That is a warning about a second pols, not a record of one. HIS-110 is the second article. It covers records written on another pols, which can be read only there, and the loss of a record if a pols drops out. Neither article mentions a hulpslag or a kristalresonator. ENG-011, ENG-102, and ENG-103 are not in my source, so I cannot confirm or deny the Engineer's account of them.

**(b) Day 10, 02:40:** My source has no entry at 02:40 and therefore neither confirms nor denies it. The nearest entries are:
- HIS-035: "de Burchtader stokte even, gemeld door de nachtwake." gebeurd_op dag 10 04:45; vastgelegd_op dag 10 07:20.
- HIS-036: "klacht uit de benedenstad: berichten half aangekomen." gebeurd_op dag 10 04:50; vastgelegd_op dag 9 23:55.

**(c) Timing rule:** The rule is stated in HIS-103: "vastgelegd_op altijd gelijk aan gebeurd_op." It does not cover HIS-036. There, vastgelegd_op (dag 9 23:55) precedes gebeurd_op (dag 10 04:50), and HIS-035 also differs by about 2h35m. HIS-103 is contradicted by these two entries. HIS-112 and HIS-116 attribute timestamp errors on days 10 and 22 to clerks, but that is their attribution, not a verified cause. HIS-053 (dag 22 04:15 gebeurd, dag 22 01:50 vastgelegd) shows the same pattern. I cannot establish from my source whether the register or the clock is at fault. HIS-036 must be checked against the original logs before anyone relies on its timestamps.

beurten.vraag: Please state the content of each record you cited but did not describe, individually: (1) ENG-119, the charter. Quote its article numbers or clauses, and state which one governs hulpslag activation, its authorization, and the tempo rules. (2) ENG-063, ENG-064, ENG-065 and ENG-066, separately. For each, give the date, time, the values recorded, and whether it shows any activation, versterking or fijnregeling change. (3) Does any record in your source name who may authorize a hulpslag activation, or set a condition for it (for example, a requirement to inform the Kroonklok)? Cite the exact record ID for each.
beurten.reden: The Engineer cited ENG-119 and ENG-063 to ENG-066 as the routine-check and charter basis for the hulpslag but never stated their content, and the activation trigger and authorization rule (Pillar 1 and Pillar 2) remain unsourced. ENG-105's 'hogerhand' is the only authorization hint and no other role can verify it. One targeted turn is needed to unpack these records individually before stopping. The cross-file claim that the hulpslag exists separately from the Kroonklok cannot be resolved by any other role, because the Historian's HIS-109 and HIS-110 are not in the Engineer's source.
open_vragen: Who authorized the hulpslag activation at day 10 02:40? No source names an authorizer; ENG-105 says only 'hogerhand'.
What do ENG-063, ENG-064, ENG-065, ENG-066 (routine check logs) and ENG-119 (charter) actually state, article by article?

beurten.tekst:
**(1) ENG-119 (werkboek, dag 13): not a charter.** My source contains no charter, article numbers, or clauses for the hulpslag. ENG-119 is a note on routine checks: "De routinecontrole van de hulpslag op papier gezet, zodat iemand anders ze kan doen als ik ziek ben: resonator afstoffen, temperatuur van de versterker aflezen, de lampjes tellen, alles noteren." It governs no activation, authorization, or tempo. The closest tempo guidance is ENG-114 (dag 12), a personal note: versterking gives "meer doorvoer, het tempo blijft gelijk", fijnregeling adjusts tempo "in stappen van 0,1%", and "Bijsturen hoeft niet."

**(2) Installatielog entries.** Each is component hulpslag, action routinecontrole, status ok. None records any values.
- **ENG-063:** dag 13, 09:00. No activation, versterking, or fijnregeling change.
- **ENG-064:** dag 17, 09:15. Same.
- **ENG-065:** dag 21, 09:30. Same.
- **ENG-066:** dag 29, 09:45. Same.

The log does not record the readings that ENG-119 describes (resonator, versterker temperature, lamps). I have no values for any of these dates.

**(3) Authorization.** No record in my source names who may authorize a hulpslag activation, and none sets a precondition for it.
- **ENG-105** (dag 9): "Goedkeuring verkregen van hogerhand." No authorizer is named. The only condition is "Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait."
- **ENG-011** (dag 10, 02:40): "geactiveerd: eigen pols voor het datanet, los van de Kroonklok." This describes the pulse as separate. It names no authorizer and does not require informing the Kroonklok.
- **ENG-106** (dag 10): activation at 02:40, no authorizer named.
- **ENG-103** (dag 4): "Als dit werkt" is design intent, not authority.
- **ENG-010** (dag 9, 16:45) and **ENG-008** (dag 8, 14:10) record the proefopstelling and the delivered parts, with no authorizer.

I have no record of a rule requiring the Kroonklok to be informed. I cannot confirm the "tweede pols" warning cited by the Historian (HIS-109), because those IDs are not in my source.

beurten.reden: Stopping early. All six roles have spoken, and the four pillars are substantiated as far as the sources allow. Pillar 1: the hulpslag activation at day 10 02:40 is recorded only by the Engineer (ENG-011, ENG-106); no source names an authorizer, and the only pointer is ENG-105 'hogerhand'. Pillar 2: the governing rules are cited individually (HIS-102, HIS-103, HIS-109, HIS-110, GUA-102 to GUA-108, ARC-110), so no range collapse needs unpacking. Pillar 3: the four-day rhythm is confirmed by BEA-113 and ORA-130 with onsets on days 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34, 38 and 42, which gives a calculated next date of day 46; the Oracle's day-33 severity claim (ORA-121) is refuted by BEA-071 and ARC-114. Pillar 4: the recovery constraints are in HIS-110, GUA-106 and ARC-109. Contradictions: the Engineer's separate hulpslag versus the Historian's single pols (HIS-102, HIS-109) cannot be verified cross-file, and further turns would only repeat that impasse. The day 10 and day 22 timestamp inversions (HIS-035, HIS-036, HIS-053) are attributed to clerks but unverified. GUA-115 (01:50 archive entry) matches HIS-053 (01:50 vastgelegd) for day 22, which points to a register timing error and needs no further turn. The day 22 packet loss at 04:15 (ENG-026) has no independent record. Source-absent items are pruned.

beurten.tekst: Council consensus: the disturbance began on day 10 at 04:45 and recurred on a four-day rhythm through day 42, the latest observed incident day. The only recorded intervention before onset is the separate hulpslag pulse, activated on day 10 at 02:40 and boosted at 03:00, under an approval attributed to 'hogerhand' with no named authorizer. Resolved disputes: no cable change occurred (ENG-003, HIS-014, BEA-115), the conjunction theory is rejected because heavy nights began before the stars converged (ORA-112, ORA-110), and no outside breach is evidenced because seals were intact after inside openings (GUA-044, GUA-105). Timestamp errors in the Historian register contradict its own rule and must be checked against originals. Recovery sequence: preserve and copy records, verify timestamps, deactivate the hulpslag, shut down the datanet on Archmage advice, reverse the day 24 pols change, identify the authorizer, extend shield patrols into the 03:00 to 06:00 window, and measure leylijnen on each incident date. Forecast: next recurrence on day 46 if unaddressed.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether a separate hulpslag pulse was activated on day 10 at 02:40 and could be the source of the disturbance.

standpunten.engineer: The hulpslag was activated on day 10 at 02:40, running separately from the Kroonklok, and raised throughput at 03:00 (ENG-011, ENG-012).
standpunten.historian: No second pols or hulpslag is recorded in the Historian's source; HIS-109 warns against a second pols but does not record one, and the Engineer's IDs cannot be confirmed.

geschillen.uitkomst: The activation is recorded only by the Engineer, and the Historian reports no record rather than a denial. Its timing matches the onset of heavy nights at 04:45 on day 10 (ORA-110), so the hulpslag is the leading intervention candidate, but the desync link remains a working hypothesis until verified.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether the woudkabels were changed before day 10, which the Beast Master raised as a cause.

standpunten.beast_master: The tower laid new cables in the woud, and that is the cause (BEA-109); the Beast Master's own source records only a 'controle' on day 3 (BEA-102).
standpunten.engineer: Woudkabels were inspected on day 3 and not changed (ENG-003).
standpunten.historian: The cables were laid 23 years ago and have not been changed, moved or replaced (HIS-007, HIS-105); the day 3 inspection recorded niets gewijzigd (HIS-014).

geschillen.uitkomst: No cable change is recorded. The Engineer and Historian both record no change, and the Beast Master itself records only cables still present on day 27 (BEA-115) and reports that the tower denied new cables (BEA-109). The cable claim is unsupported inference and is rejected.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether a planetary conjunction caused the disturbance, as the Oracle proposed.

standpunten.oracle: The Wachtsterren conjunction is the cause and the night of day 33 is the most severe (ORA-121); the rhythm is counted but no conjunction sign is recorded for the heavy nights (ORA-130).
standpunten.archmage: The Burchtader was calm during the Wachtsterren conjunction night (ARC-114), and Sterrenwacht confirms the next conjunction on day 33 (ARC-111).
standpunten.beast_master: The Oracle named the night of day 33 the most severe, but the animals were calm that night (BEA-118, BEA-071).

geschillen.uitkomst: The conjunction theory is rejected. Heavy nights began on day 10, before the stars converged (ORA-112, first noted on day 12), and the day 33 night was calm for the animals and the Burchtader (BEA-071, ARC-114, ORA-133). The recurrence is a four-day rhythm, not conjunction-based.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether an outside breach, hackers or infiltrants caused the shield openings.

standpunten.guardian_keeper: The openings on day 10 and day 22 were from inside with seals intact and no outside breach seen (GUA-019, GUA-043, GUA-044); the tower's hacker claim (GUA-115) and the infiltrant claim (GUA-116) have no supporting record, and the shields show no defect (GUA-120).
standpunten.engineer: The day 22 packet loss at poort oost was recorded at 04:15 (ENG-026), the same time as the inside opening at GUA-043; the Engineer's source does not establish a cause for the packet loss.

geschillen.uitkomst: No outside breach is evidenced. Seals break only from outside (GUA-105), so intact seals after inside openings rule out external forcing, and the hacker and infiltrant claims are unsupported. The shared 04:15 timing points to an internal event.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether the firewall was tightened on day 22 at 04:20.

standpunten.engineer: The firewall was tightened at 04:20 on day 22 after the packet loss (ENG-027).
standpunten.guardian_keeper: The Guardian Keeper's source names no firewall change and does not contain ENG-027, so it neither confirms nor denies the change.

geschillen.uitkomst: Only the Engineer records the firewall change; the Guardian reports no record, which is not a denial. The change is recorded, but its causal link to the packet loss is not established.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether the timestamps in the Historian register are reliable and whether the guardian archive timing is accurate.

standpunten.historian: The rule vastgelegd_op equals gebeurd_op holds (HIS-103), but HIS-035, HIS-036 and HIS-053 contradict it; clerks are blamed for the errors (HIS-112, HIS-116), which the Historian does not treat as verified.
standpunten.guardian_keeper: The archive recorded the guards' report at 01:50 on day 22, over two hours before the 04:15 opening, so the timing should be checked (GUA-115).

geschillen.uitkomst: The register rule HIS-103 is contradicted by HIS-035, HIS-036 and HIS-053, and the Guardian's 01:50 entry shows a similar timing problem. The clerk attribution is unverified. The timestamps cannot be relied on until checked against originals.

geschillen.onderwerp: Whether the leylijnen have a history of hapering, which the Historian and Archmage record differently.

standpunten.historian: No leylijn hapering in 23 years of datanet operation (HIS-106).
standpunten.archmage: Low readings of sterkte 3.1 to 4.6 on day 14 and 3.1 to 4.8 on day 42 are recorded and attributed to the datanet (ARC-015, ARC-028, ARC-071, ARC-084, ARC-109, ARC-116).

geschillen.uitkomst: The Archmage's dated measurements on day 14 and day 42 are direct records and stand. The Historian's HIS-106 is an absence statement from its archive and does not account for those readings, so it does not deny the measurements.

geschillen.onderwerp: Who authorized the hulpslag activation on day 9 and day 10.

standpunten.engineer: ENG-105 (day 9) cites approval from hogerhand with the instruction not to publicize it, and ENG-106 records activation at 02:40 with no authorizer named.
standpunten.historian: No authorizer is named for day 9 or day 10; the day 9 entries HIS-032, HIS-033 and HIS-034 do not concern the datanet.
